chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Zawad narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Shazan narrated to us, saying: Al-Walid ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Makhool ibn Zakvan narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Sirin, from Jabir ibn Samurah al-Sawa'i, saying:

I was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and he said: 'This matter will be led by twelve.' He said: 'The people made noise, so I could not hear what he said. I asked my father, who was closer to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) than I was, saying: 'What did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say?' He said: 'He said: They are all from Quraysh, and they do not resemble one another.'

key_terms.لَا يَرَىٰ مِثْلَهُ: Do not resemble one another (distinct from each other)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of the twelve leaders after him?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Khisal establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve Imams, a core tenet of Shia eschatology and political theology. The phrase 'each unlike the other' (لا يرى مثله) is interpreted by Shia scholars as indicating their unique, distinct qualities or the specific divine attributes bestowed upon each Imam, distinguishing them from one another despite their shared lineage. This narration serves as a primary scriptural basis for the concept of Ijma' (consensus) regarding the twelve successors, linking the prophetic tradition directly to the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt.
